zebralogic.title: Assign fixed‑position attributes immediately
zebralogic.principle: When a clue directly ties an attribute to a specific house number, assign that attribute at the start. This reduces the search space and prevents later contradictions caused by ambiguous placement.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a house index (e.g., "Peter is in the third house" or "the white house is the fifth house").
zebralogic.example: Leaving Peter unassigned to house 3, later causing a conflict with other distance clues.

zebralogic.title: Translate direct adjacency into offset constraints
zebralogic.principle: Clues using "directly left of" or "directly right of" imply an exact offset of one house. Encode them as X = Y − 1 or X = Y + 1 to enforce strict adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains the phrase "directly left of" or "directly right of".
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "directly left of" as merely "somewhere left of", allowing X to be any house left of Y.

zebralogic.title: Merge consecutive adjacency clues into chains
zebralogic.principle: If several clues link attributes via direct adjacency (e.g., A left of B and B left of C), combine them into a single chain. This forces the involved attributes to occupy consecutive houses and dramatically narrows possible start positions.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When multiple clues describe direct left‑right relationships among different attributes.
zebralogic.example: Treating "volleyball left of baseball" and "baseball left of brown hair" separately, failing to enforce that they occupy three consecutive houses.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: A clue stating "N houses between X and Y" means the absolute positional difference is N + 1. Convert the wording into |pos(X) − pos(Y)| = N + 1 to avoid off‑by‑one errors.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a specific number of houses between two items.
zebralogic.example: Reading "two houses between green and Bob" as a distance of two houses, placing them only one house apart.

zebralogic.title: Bind equivalence clues to the same house
zebralogic.principle: When a clue equates two attributes (e.g., "the pizza lover is the rock‑music lover"), treat them as a single combined attribute for that house. This prevents assigning the linked values to different houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue states that two different attribute types belong to the same person.
zebralogic.example: Assigning pizza to house 2 and rock music to house 4, ignoring the clue that they must be the same person.

zebralogic.title: Treat "somewhere left/right of" as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Phrases like "X is somewhere to the left of Y" only require pos(X) < pos(Y); they do not imply adjacency. Encode them as strict inequalities without a fixed offset.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses "somewhere to the left/right of" rather than "directly".
zebralogic.example: Assuming Arnold must be immediately left of the blue lover, restricting placements unnecessarily.

zebralogic.title: Apply exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: Clues that forbid an attribute from a particular house (e.g., "tennis is not in the fifth house") must be used to eliminate that house from the attribute's candidate set.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains a negation such as "not" or "does not".
zebralogic.example: Placing tennis in house 5 despite the clue that tennis is not in the fifth house.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once. After assigning a value to a house, remove it from the candidate lists of all other houses and check for duplicates.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Throughout the solving process, after any assignment or elimination.
zebralogic.example: Giving the hair colour brown to both house 4 and house 5, violating the one‑per‑category rule.

zebralogic.title: Leverage ordering chains from multiple inequality clues
zebralogic.principle: Combine several left/right clues that share attributes into a partial order (e.g., coffee < milk < hip‑hop). This ordering narrows the set of feasible positions for each involved attribute.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When multiple inequality clues involve overlapping attributes.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring the chain coffee < milk < hip‑hop, resulting in coffee being placed to the right of milk.

zebralogic.title: Continuously verify consistency after each deduction
zebralogic.principle: After each assignment or elimination, check all clues for violations. If any clue is broken, backtrack or revise the recent deduction before proceeding.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After every step in the deduction process.
zebralogic.example: Proceeding with assignments that later conflict with the "white house is the fifth house" clue without revisiting earlier choices.

zebralogic.description: Treating "somewhere left of" as adjacency (directly left)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model conflates the word "somewhere" with "directly", turning a loose inequality into a strict offset.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Encode "somewhere left of" as pos(X) < pos(Y) without requiring adjacency; only "directly left of" should enforce a one‑house offset.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting "N houses between" as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The phrasing is misread as the two items being N houses apart, forgetting that the count excludes the endpoints.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue says "N houses between X and Y", enforce |pos(X) − pos(Y)| = N + 1.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats linked attributes as independent, leading to contradictory placements.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Whenever a clue equates two attributes (e.g., "pizza lover is rock‑music lover"), merge them into a single combined attribute for that house.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The solver fails to track that each attribute value must appear exactly once, allowing duplicates across houses.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After assigning a value, remove it from all other houses' candidate sets and constantly check that no value appears twice.

zebralogic.description: Assuming a fixed direction for "next to each other" clues
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model interprets adjacency as having a specific left‑right order, halving the possible arrangements and causing contradictions.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Represent "next to each other" as an unordered adjacency constraint: pos(A) = pos(B) ± 1.
